stem: Why is the prompt treatment of impetigo specifically emphasized in Australian Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities?

options.text: To prevent the high mortality associated with neonatal sepsis
To reduce the risk of triggering acute rheumatic fever and heart disease
To stop the spread of antibiotic-resistant \textit{Escherichia coli}
To ensure children do not develop permanent dental decay

explanation: Skin infections caused by Group A \textit{Streptococcus} are believed to be a major trigger for rheumatic fever in these high-prevalence areas.
rationale: Consider the systemic inflammatory condition that can follow an untreated streptococcal skin infection.

optionExplanations.A: While sepsis is serious, the specific community-wide focus for impetigo is related to a long-term cardiac complication.
optionExplanations.B: Skin infections caused by Group A \textit{Streptococcus} are believed to be a major trigger for rheumatic fever in these high-prevalence areas.
optionExplanations.C: Impetigo is caused by \textit{Streptococcus} or \textit{Staphylococcus}, not \textit{E. coli}.
optionExplanations.D: Dental disease is a separate morbidity concern caused by factors like fermentable carbohydrates and \textit{S. mutants}.
